title: Cottage Cheese vs Greek Yogurt: Protein, Calories and Key Differences

seo.title: Cottage Cheese vs Greek Yogurt: Protein and Calories
seo.meta_description: Both provide about 10–12 g protein/100 g. Nonfat Greek yogurt is usually lower in calories and sodium; cottage cheese can deliver more protein in a larger serving.
seo.search_intent: Compare cottage cheese and Greek yogurt for protein, calories, fat, sodium and serving size.

excerpt: Cottage cheese and Greek yogurt are both high-protein dairy foods and are quite close: each often provides around 10–12 grams of protein per 100 grams. The bigger difference is sodium, with cottage cheese often several times higher. Calories depend on fat level, and typical serving size can change total protein more than the small per-100-gram gap.
content_html:
Cottage cheese and Greek yogurt often compete for the same breakfast or snack role: a lot of protein in a relatively small portion and an easy base for fruit, nuts or savory toppings. If protein is the only metric, there is not much reason to crown a winner.

Per 100 grams they are usually around 10–12 grams of protein. The large difference is sodium, while calories depend much more on fat level than on the product name.

A comparison that matches fat level more fairly

To keep a full-fat product from dominating the result, it helps to compare low-fat cottage cheese with plain nonfat Greek yogurt.

Per 100 gLow-fat cottage cheeseNonfat Greek yogurt
Calories~80–90~55–65
Protein~11–12 g~10 g
Fat~2–3 g<1 g
Sodium~300–450 mg~30–60 mg

Protein differs by only 1–2 grams per 100 grams. Sodium is a completely different story: cottage cheese can contain six, eight or even ten times as much depending on the brand.

Serving size changes total protein more than the small density gap

A roughly 7-ounce serving of cottage cheese can provide around 22–24 grams of protein. A 6-ounce container of nonfat Greek yogurt often provides about 17 grams.

That does not make cottage cheese dramatically more protein-dense. It mostly reflects the fact that cottage cheese is often eaten in a somewhat larger serving. Match the serving weight and the gap narrows.

Calories follow the fat level you choose

Nonfat Greek yogurt can sit near 60 calories per 100 grams, while whole Greek yogurt may approach 90–100. Some low-fat cottage cheeses fall right in that same range.

Cottage cheese also comes in richer versions. Before deciding one is “more fattening,” check whether the products actually have comparable fat content.

Sodium is the difference people are most likely to miss

Salt is commonly added during cottage-cheese production, and it shows up clearly on the label. A 7-ounce serving can exceed 600–800 mg of sodium in some brands.

Plain Greek yogurt generally contains far less, often around 30–60 mg per 100 grams. For someone trying to limit sodium, that gap may matter far more than gaining one or two extra grams of protein.

They are also made differently

Greek yogurt starts with bacterial fermentation and is then concentrated. Depending on the product and any later heat treatment, it may contain live cultures.

Cottage cheese is a fresh curd cheese. It should not automatically be assumed to have the same live-culture profile, although some brands add cultures.

What about calcium?

There is no universal winner. Calcium can be lost with whey drainage in cottage cheese, and some Greek yogurts lose calcium during straining too. Brand-to-brand variation is large enough that the label is more useful than a blanket rule.

Which one makes more sense?

If you want a very lean, low-sodium, high-protein option, plain nonfat Greek yogurt is hard to beat. If you prefer a savory curd texture or naturally eat a larger serving, cottage cheese can easily take you above 20 grams of protein.

They are too close in protein for a tiny numerical lead to decide the choice. Sodium, fat level, texture and serving size are much more useful differences.

faq.question: Which has more protein, cottage cheese or Greek yogurt?
faq.answer: Per 100 grams they are usually close at about 10–12 grams. Total protein depends heavily on serving size.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Nonfat Greek yogurt usually has fewer than low-fat cottage cheese, but full-fat versions can change the comparison.

faq.question: Which has more sodium?
faq.answer: Cottage cheese usually contains far more sodium than plain Greek yogurt.
